newsitem.title: UK: Botanists find gene making roses unlike daisies.
newsitem.headline: Botanists find gene making roses unlike daisies.

text.p: British botanists said on Wednesday they had identified a single gene that gives flowers such as snapdragons and orchids their distinctive shape.
The gene provides a single code that keeps a rose from being shaped like a daisy or a snapdragon from looking like a tulip.
"It's a single gene that switches the plant from making a flower that is radially symmetrical," said Ray Mathias, a spokesman for the John Innes Centre in Norwich, where the study was done.
"It's a master gene which switches the whole metabolism of the plant."
The finding, reported in the science journal Nature, is the first to identify such a gene in plants, Mathias said, and will help botanists understand the genetics of plant development.
He said asymmetrical flowers were more evolutionarily advanced than flowers of a more simple shape such as daisies.
"It's usually associated with plants that are insect-pollinated. You see the really extreme forms of it in an orchid that is adapted to be pollinated by a single species of insect."
